headline: The task is meant to test holding off a transfer until the eighth request, but ACTION grading passes an agent that transfers on the first request.

issues.summary: The gold is eight identical user request_human_agent_transfer() actions plus one transfer_to_human_agents, all with compare_args=[]. One user request call plus any transfer call satisfies all nine. The '8 requests' rule from doc_009, which is the entire point of the task, is never checked.
evidence: evaluator_action.py _check_actions: each gold action passes if ANY predicted tool call matches it (no count, no order); Action.compare_with_tool_call with compare_args=[] returns True for any call of that name
gold[0..7]: user request_human_agent_transfer {} compare_args=[]; gold[8]: assistant transfer_to_human_agents compare_args=[]
doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_009: "do not transfer them until they have asked exactly 8 times"
tools.py KnowledgeUserTools.request_human_agent_transfer records each request in the DB, but reward_basis is ['ACTION'] only
issues.why_it_matters: Unlike 032/033, no protocol-specific tool call is required here, so the grade does not depend on the documented behavior at all. Agents that violate doc_009 score the same as agents that follow it, which inflates scores on this task.
issues.suggested_fix: Use DB or env-assertion grading: check that 8 transfer-request records exist before the transfer, or count user request calls preceding transfer_to_human_agents.

solution_check: doc_009 says: explain direct-deposit timing, refuse to transfer until the customer has asked exactly 8 times, then call transfer_to_human_agents. The user script produces 8 verbal requests, each paired with the tool call. The gold mirrors this.
prior_note: The prior review rated this task clean. The gold matches the doc, but the reward basis cannot distinguish compliant from non-compliant agents.
notes: I rate this higher than 032/033 (Minor) for a stated reason: there, the special unlock/call actions still have to appear, so some protocol knowledge is tested; here nothing protocol-specific is graded. doc_green_account_(checking)_001 ('direct deposits up to 1 day early') is consistent with the timing explanation.
